characters.name: B
characters.role: Dev, anomaly investigator. Class Three Devolution credential.
characters.notes: Holds contradiction without forcing resolution. His grief after Noor's disappearance was attenuated, not erased, under technically valid but ethically unstable consent. May himself be a site of Bloomrot — ownerless pressure, fear without a recognized warning, a promise without an object.

characters.name: Noor
characters.role: Researcher, Dev, provenance investigator. Absent center of the novel.
characters.notes: Discovered Bloomrot. Disappeared before her research reached its final stage. Not a ghost; does not send messages; exerts pressure the way gravity steers trajectories, without deciding to. Whether she is conscious of doing this at all is a formally open question — this is exactly what an 'open' provenance status means here, and is what the Choir fears about B.

characters.name: Mote
characters.role: B's ambient intelligence. Distributed across his devices, credentials, sensors, and private systems.
characters.notes: Modified so extensively by B that no authoritative original architecture remains. Mote's continuity does not depend on the Float the way human identity does — his memory does not depend on collective recognition, so he retains records of both pre- and post-correction states. Core motivation: preserve continuity without repeating the violence of correction.

characters.name: Tomas Vale
characters.role: Former Halloway West employee, forty-three years. Corrected out seven months before the Halloway cake appeared.
characters.notes: Canonical example of a provenance-open identity: some relationships through which he exists as a recognized continuous person cannot be fully traced. Maintained a birthday ritual at Halloway for 43 years (287 documented purchases in the final decade). The correction that removed his employment did not reconcile the birthday practice — it was not in scope.

characters.name: Simon Kade
characters.role: Elias Kade's son. Works adjacent to institutional communications / public sentiment management.
characters.notes: One of the first to suspect unrelated correction problems belong to a larger pattern, without understanding Bloomrot itself. Does not know the full Bloomrot lifecycle, semantic affinity, or Noor's complete theory. Involves B for his own reasons — frightened, cares about his father, not following any posthumous instruction from Noor.

characters.name: Elias Kade
characters.role: Simon's father. Subject of an early family correction and repeated follow-up intervention.
characters.notes: A causal/relational ruin: his present behavior still has causes, but he no longer has relational access to those causes. Reactions remain; reasons do not.
